messages.author: 4930488f69589d77
messages.subject: Clarification of model type/description
parts:
In JAGS/BUGS  the precision (1/variance) in a linear regression may be expressed explicitly with a distribution based on epsilon (Model 1) or as in Model 2. Do these different parameterization have specific names?  If so is there a reference? Thanks!
Dan

Model 1
#likelihood
for (i in 1:n){
        y[i] <- a + b*x[i] + epsilon[i]
        epsilon[i]~dnorm(0,tau)
}
#priors and constraints
a~dnorn(0,0.001)
b~dnorm(0,0.001)
tau<-1/(sig*sig)
sig~dnorm(0,0.01)T(0,)

or 

Model 2
#likelihood
for (i in 1:n){
        y[i]~dnorm(a + b*x[i],tau)
        }

#priors and constraints
a~dnorn(0,0.001)
b~dnorm(0,0.001)
tau<-1/(sig*sig)
sig~dnorm(0,0.01)T(0,)

messages.author: dd632bd3bbcdd7e9
messages.subject: Re: Clarification of model type/description
parts:
Hi Dan,
Those are called centered vs uncentered parameterizations.
Here is a paper explaining how neither one is universally the best choice: https://www.tandfonline.com/doi/abs/10.1198/jcgs.2011.203main
-Perry

I thought uncentered parameterization would be:

messages.author: dd632bd3bbcdd7e9
messages.subject: Re: Clarification of model type/description
parts:
Oh I see I was a bit hasty.

I usually see this come up for random effects, where one can give it mean zero and add it to other terms or center it around the mean of other terms.  And then it would enter into the mean of a datum or some similar role.  So I was interpreting this as a code snippet.  But I think you're right: if y[i] are the data, then I'm not seeing how Model 1 could make sense.  The data wouldn't be informing the parameters, unless there is something else not shown?

Matt, I'm not sure of the different ways terms are used, but I would have called your example a scaling issue.  I looked back at this earlier reference (https://doi.org/10.1093/biomet/82.3.479) and I think the centered vs uncentered (or non-centered) terms were established for setting up random effects with mean zero vs building them up centered around other terms.  I would be glad to hear of other ways terms have been used.

-Perry

Matt,
You are correct regarding normal linear regression. It's been a long day and I have been working with count data using the log link. I have simulated data and both models return simulated values. Model 1 should have been:

model{

#likelihood
for (i in 1:n){

y[i]~dpois(lambda[i])
  log(lambda[i])<- log_lambda[i]
  log_lambda[i]<- alpha + beta*x[i]+eps[i]
  eps[i]~dnorm(0,tau)
}

alpha~dnorm(0,0.001)
beta~dnorm(0,0.001)
sig~dnorm(0,001)T(0,)
tau<- 1/sig*sig
sig2<- sig*sig
}

Model 2 should have been:
model{

#likelihood
for (i in 1:n){

y[i]~dpois(lambda[i])
  log(lambda[i])<- log_lambda[i]
  log_lambda[i]~dnorm(alpha + beta*x[i],tau)
}

alpha~dnorm(0,0.001)
beta~dnorm(0,0.001)
sig~dnorm(0,001)T(0,)
tau<- 1/sig*sig
sig2<- sig*sig
}
